solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flower with interior unattractive, not half, and crinkly

indicators.note: the flower is given an interior, so the other piece sits inside it
only half of the word for unattractive is kept, its second half dropped

explanation.surface: A gardener describes an ugly flower whose middle has shrivelled and crinkled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps only the front half of UGLY; 'with interior' tells you the flower holds that piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and medical word meaning wrinkled or ridged, a close synonym of crinkly.

clue.text: Careless soldiers with assignments only 50% completed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: only half of the word for assignments is finished, so its back half is dropped

explanation.surface: An officer complains that troops are slapdash, finishing only half their tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duties, a direct synonym of careless.

clue.text: One moving one's arms badly

parts.note: seems to describe someone flailing clumsily, but arms are weapons and badly means illegally: a smuggler of weapons

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a poor dancer waving their arms; the arms are guns, moved unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of firearms transports weapons illegally, which is moving arms in a bad way.

clue.text: Wise Men were doing this to do this!

definitions.text: Wise Men were doing this to do this!

parts.words: Wise Men were doing this to do this!
parts.note: the Magi were searching in order to visit the newborn king; split differently

explanation.walkthrough: The Magi travelled looking for Jesus so as to see the King: the answer is both what they were doing and, split in two, why.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wise Men were searching for the child, which was their purpose: to behold a monarch.

clue.text: Compound in which revolutionary leader seems to be self-absorbed!

indicators.note: the man is shown absorbing himself: his first name is taken into his surname

parts.note: Tom Paine was a leading figure of the American Revolution

explanation.surface: A chemist jokes that a famous radical seems wrapped up in himself.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM is moved inside PAINE, so Paine literally absorbs his own self.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are nitrogen compounds formed when protein putrefies, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Problem about coach that gets fouled up with wet brown stuff

definitions.text: that gets fouled up with wet brown stuff

indicators.note: the word for problem goes around the word for coach

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A trainer's trouble seems to be a coach getting covered in mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The wet brown stuff sounds like mud on a sports coach; it is used tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer for tea catches the soggy leaves, so it becomes clogged with damp brown matter.

clue.text: Something heard on instrument that's certainly a feature of concert

definitions.meaning: a note played on a piano or other keyboard instrument

definitions.text: that's certainly a feature of concert
definitions.meaning: the central letter of the word concert is a C

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the seven-letter word concert has C as its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The note at the centre of the piano keyboard is a familiar pitch, and the letter in the middle of concert is C.

clue.text: Greek bond may be this

definitions.meaning: relating to Ionia, an ancient Greek region, its dialect or its order of columns
in chemistry a bond formed by electrostatic attraction between charged particles

explanation.definitionFit: Ionian Greeks gave their name to a column order and dialect; a chemical bond between charged ions has the same adjective.

clue.text: Tough times with English pretending to be outsiders

indicators.note: English and pretending stand outside, with times put between them

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: Hard days for an English actor playing someone from beyond the circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'to be outsiders' has E and ACTING enclose X.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task is demanding, so tough is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Female author's shelf

definitions.meaning: Hilary ..., the English novelist who wrote Wolf Hall

explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel was a twice Booker-winning novelist, and the word also names the ledge over a hearth.

clue.text: Where one finds Italians beginning to sing song to drown noise

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word sing is taken
the song swallows up the noise, which sits inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: Opera singers drowning out a racket, the sort of scene one expects among Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is an island region of Italy, so its people are Italians.

clue.text: Pull one into vigorous fight with determination

indicators.note: the pieces for pull and one go into the word for vigorous

parts.note: stout can mean strong and vigorous
to lug is to pull or haul
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drags a person into a hard brawl with grim resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest something to the finish, trading blows, is an idiom for fighting it out doggedly.

clue.text: Ray is this when becoming stray, destitute

definitions.text: Ray is this when becoming stray
definitions.meaning: the word ray turns into stray when the street abbreviation ST is placed in front of it

explanation.walkthrough: ST is the abbreviation for street; put ST on RAY and it becomes STRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homeless and living rough is described by this idiom, which matches being destitute.

clue.text: Legal officer's housed here in Paris

indicators.note: the officer has the French word housed inside, so it goes within

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A legal officer has lodgings in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the officer has the French word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means permitted by law, a formal synonym of lawful.

clue.text: Batsman going up the order gets guard

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a lower-order batsman sent in early near the close of play to protect the better batsmen
someone keeping watch through the dark hours

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a weak batsman is promoted late in the day to survive until stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A security watchman on duty overnight guards premises, and cricket uses the same title for a promoted tail-ender.

clue.text: A supreme little university managed to meet the required standard

indicators.note: the letters are managed, that is handled and rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A top student at a small university succeeds in reaching the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be good enough or to reach expectations is the meaning of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Nasty mince pies one rejected as taster

indicators.note: nasty pies suggests the letters are spoilt and jumbled
the letter for one is thrown out of the pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a horrible Christmas pie after a trial bite.
explanation.walkthrough: MINCE PIES less I (one 'rejected') is rearranged ('Nasty') to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample, and a sample taken for examination is a specimen.

clue.text: Soldier sent to Rhine with a pal, moving bits of equipment

indicators.note: the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A paratrooper is posted to the Rhine with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphernalia means miscellaneous articles and gear, the various items of kit one needs.

clue.text: Thinking dear old lover should be got rid of

indicators.note: the former partner is to be removed from the word for dear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a costly former partner should be dumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive describes someone deep in thought, so it matches thinking used as an adjective.

clue.text: Insecticide desperate man put down in row

indicators.note: in a down clue the man is placed within the row

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic man sprays bug killer along a row of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a cowboy character in the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindane is an organochlorine pesticide used against insects, now widely banned.

clue.text: Singer is performer getting a bit confused initially about name

indicators.note: the muddled word goes about the letter for name
only the start of the performer's word is muddled, its opening two letters swapped

explanation.surface: A vocalist turned actor gets a little mixed up at first about a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused initially' swaps the first two letters of ACTOR to make CATOR, which goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor is the official who leads the singing in a synagogue or church choir.

clue.text: Gang of women, any number going after old British chap

parts.note: cove is dated British slang for a man
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A group of women, however many, follows an old-fashioned English gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, traditionally female, so a gang of women in a mocking sense.

clue.text: As composer, I had member of the clergy uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are lifted, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: I'd is a contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A priest says his spirits were raised as a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: IDREV read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Arachnid? A naturalist is put off, surprisingly

indicators.note: the remaining letters are rearranged in a surprising way
these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A wildlife expert is unexpectedly repelled by a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IS from A NATURALIST and rearrange the rest. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, one example of an arachnid.

clue.text: One may offer the ultimate in punishment in a term that becomes awful

definitions.text: One may offer the ultimate in punishment in a term that becomes awful

indicators.note: the words become awful, so they are jumbled
the last letter of the word punishment

explanation.surface: A strict disciplinarian hands out the harshest penalty, making a school term miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A TERM rearranged plus T from 'the ultimate in punishment'; the whole clue also describes a stern disciplinarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian who imposes harsh punishment for small faults.

clue.text: Notice army retreating behind hiding-place?

parts.note: a cave is somewhere to hide

indicators.note: the army goes back, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A notice warns that soldiers are falling back behind a hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is a standard abbreviation for Britain's volunteer reserve; 'retreating' turns it round and 'behind' puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or formal notice, typically a caution attached to a statement.

clue.text: Rose is sweet

definitions.meaning: a type of climbing rose bred in the 19th century

explanation.definitionFit: Noisette names both a class of climbing roses and a chocolate made with hazelnuts.

clue.text: Modify tendency to fly off the handle

definitions.meaning: to moderate or tone something down

definitions.text: tendency to fly off the handle

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to moderate; as a noun it is a disposition to lose one's composure.
